title: New CI quality gate failed on pre-existing formatting, typing, and Bandit findings
summary: The first run of the CI quality gate failed four jobs: Prettier found 3 unformatted files, Ruff format found 12 files to reformat, mypy found 9 type errors, and Bandit reported B310 for urlopen without a URL scheme restriction.
recommendation: Bring the existing code into compliance in the same change that enables a new check: format with Prettier and Ruff, fix the reported mypy errors, and restrict urlopen to http(s) URLs before suppressing B310.
evidence: Format (Prettier)	Check Markdown, YAML, and JSON formatting	2026-10-23T16:42:11.1942883Z [warn] Code style issues found in 3 files. Run Prettier with --write to fix.
Lint (Ruff)	Ruff format check	2026-10-23T16:42:10.9226749Z 12 files would be reformatted, 22 files already formatted
Security (Bandit)	Run Bandit	2026-10-23T16:42:13.8758687Z >> Issue: [B310:blacklist] Audit url open for permitted schemes. Allowing use of file:/ or custom schemes is often unexpected.
Type check (mypy)	Run mypy	2026-10-23T16:42:24.2208760Z Found 9 errors in 6 files (checked 17 source files)
root_cause: Commit 43c1910 added Prettier, Ruff format, mypy, and Bandit gates without bringing the existing code into compliance: 3 files were not Prettier-formatted, 12 files were not Ruff-formatted, 6 files had 9 mypy errors, and 3 urlopen calls accepted any URL scheme (Bandit B310).

fix.description: Commit 98e39ea formatted the files with Prettier 3.9.9 and Ruff 0.16.10, fixed the 9 mypy errors, and restricted the Ollama URLs to http(s) before the urlopen calls (with a justified nosec B310).
fix.validation_evidence: Manually checked GitHub Actions run 39991021644 after fix commit 98e39ea. Prettier, Ruff, Bandit, and mypy all passed. Compared with failing run 39988949831.

title: GitHub Actions release failed updating a protected Git tag
summary: The tt-metal release workflow failed because GitHub rejected an operation on a protected Git ref. The exact tag and SHA conflict remain unconfirmed.
recommendation: Inspect the full job log and identify the actual tag and commit SHAs. Do not automatically force-move a protected release tag. If a tag points to a different commit, stop with a clear diagnostic and determine whether a new version tag is appropriate.
root_cause: Unconfirmed hypothesis: the release workflow may have attempted to update an existing protected Git tag to a different commit.

fix.description: Detect a tag-to-SHA mismatch and stop the release instead of automatically moving a protected tag.
